entries.plain: Checks that this workspace address may use your saved drafts before loading them, and asks you about a new address.
entries.summary: Keeps local-work components unmounted until the current address is admitted.
details: Reads workspace and account identity from the ready replica, then checks the local trusted-address record. The gate shows checking, explicit approval, saving or retryable error before mounting drafts/search-history consumers.
Approval explains that the address can access saved local work and may resume queued sends. Effects fence results to their current client/workspace/account scope.
The gate relies on the trust helper's answer and cannot compensate for an incorrectly admitted address; Q02 closed the helper's simultaneous first-registration gap.

While it waits it shows the workspace's banner across the top (such as sign-ins this device could not save) and, under its message, this computer's hosting line, so a hosted workspace that will not start still offers Manage hosting (UX-25).

entries.plain: Shows a form that a connected app or bot sends you, keeping its answers apart from any form that replaces it.
entries.summary: Renders an app-owned form with input and result lifetime bound to its view ID.
details: ViewModal keys AppForm by view.id, so a newly arriving app form starts with its own values, field errors, message and busy state.
Inputs are keyed by block and action ID and submitted as a nested payload. Validation refusal keeps the form open and focuses the first refused field.

N05 adds alive and submitting guards plus ID-bound client operations: a previous form's success, failure or dismissal cannot close or contaminate its replacement. Answers are not persisted locally and closing alone does not send a callback.

entries.plain: The list of messages in a channel, which loads older ones as you scroll and keeps your reading spot.
entries.summary: Shows bounded channel history while preserving reading and scroll position.
details: Loads initial, older and newer history through owned request tickets. A top visible message and offset anchor preserve position while prepending rows; explicit message jumps center and highlight a target.

Readers at the latest message stay pinned as content or viewport size changes; readers looking back are not pulled to the bottom, except by a send of their own, which brings them down to it as Discord and Slack do. History entries remember where a conversation was being read.

Separately renders optimistic pending sends with Retry/Discard and ephemeral app answers with dismissal/limit notices. Date dividers, an unread boundary and typing indicators make the timeline understandable.

Read acknowledgement follows a genuinely visible tail, and useRovingMessages makes the list a manageable keyboard region. The actual row count is bounded in client-core rather than claiming full DOM virtualization.

entries.plain: Shows one message with its author, time, text, files and reactions, plus the actions you are allowed to take.
entries.summary: Renders one message and its authorized actions with narrow replica subscriptions.
details: The memoized row renders author, timestamps, mrkdwn, files, reactions, thread affordances and app buttons. useMessageReferences tracks only referenced users/channels, and self identity/role controls relevant actions.

Reaction, pin and saved toggles report refused optimistic changes through a toast with a repeatable intent. Delete uses an explicit confirmation; mark unread delegates channel or thread cursor behavior to the client.

Copying text/link waits for clipboard outcome. App link buttons navigate normally while interactive buttons call the app through the server and wait for its result; permissions remain enforced by the server.

The in-place editor is a lazy chunk with an inline loading status and a recoverable failure, keeping editing code out of the entry every visit downloads. The emoji picker for a reaction is a lazy chunk too, with a dialog that says so if it cannot load.

Reply answers a message in place (Shift leaves its author unnotified) and Reply in thread opens its thread, as in Discord; inside a thread, Reply answers one of its replies. A reply shows its quote above it through ReplyQuote, and a reply that notified you is marked as a mention is.

The hover toolbar draws its icons at 18 px with a stroke of 2, beside the reaction emoji, and marks each button icon-live so its icon moves when pointed at. A saved message's bookmark takes the accent colour alone; with two text colours on the button, the stylesheet's order had left it looking unsaved.
A message of only a few emoji (onlyEmoji in lib/emoji.ts) is shown at 32 px, as Slack and Discord show one.

entries.plain: The box for editing a sent message, which keeps unsaved changes and refuses to overwrite a newer edit made meanwhile.
entries.summary: Edits a message while preserving unsaved words and the original comparison base.
details: An edit draft has its own message-specific slot and stores both text and the message text it began from, including compatibility with older plain-text drafts.
Save uses expectedText so a concurrent edit can be refused instead of being overwritten unnoticed. Formatting, preview, IME and code-block behavior match the composer.
The box and the Current message shown on an edit conflict read mentions as names; the kept {text, base} and the saved text keep their tokens. MessageItem loads the editor on first use.

entries.plain: The side panel that shows a thread's first message, its replies and a box to reply.
entries.summary: Displays a root message, paged replies and an independent reply composer.
details: Loads the root's thread through WorkspaceClient, displays optimistic replies and manages retry/discard for waiting sends.

Remembers reply reading anchors, protects current thread history from eviction and acknowledges the thread cursor when appropriate. Follow/Unfollow calls the client's thread-follow logic, which sends those requests in order (Q09).
A thread composer uses a root-specific draft key and optional also-send-to-channel choice rather than clobbering the channel composer.
It is a chunk of its own, fetched as the workspace opens and drawn directly from then on, which keeps the first download under its size limit.

entries.plain: The shared layout for the Pins, Saved and Threads panels. Each keeps itself up to date while it is open and shows more as you scroll.
entries.summary: Shares the layout and live, scroll-to-load behavior for Pins, Saved and followed Threads.
details: The generic panel renders a PagedList of server-loaded messages with row context, loading/empty/refusal state and a LoadMore end. listKey names a different list; a change of refreshKey, or of changedContent for a conversation it shows, reads it again in place (UX-08).

Pins are channel-specific, Saved spans readable conversations, and Threads represents followed conversations with unread counts and opens the thread rather than a single message. Saved refreshes on the saved set, Threads on follow state including each thread's lastSeq, so a new reply shows at once.
Since Q08 PinsPanel also passes its channel's changedContent marker in refreshKey, so a pin, edit or deletion outside the loaded timeline is seen.

entries.plain: The search window, which finds words in messages and file names. Results come straight under the box, filters are chips you add from From, In, Has and Date or by typing from:@name, and more results load as you scroll.
entries.summary: Searches server-side message text and attachment names, results first, with filters as removable chips (UX-51).
details: Under the field sit the filters in force as chips, each one click to remove, then From, In and Has menus and a Date popover (Today, Last 7 days, Last 30 days, or a day either side) to add more; a ? button shows the modifier syntax. Typed modifiers become chips through lib/searchFilters.ts. The field and chips stay above the results, which scroll, so results start within about 90 px of the field at 1280x820.

Results follow what is typed and the filters chosen a quarter-second after typing pauses, and the previous answer stays on show while the next question is out, its status line and marked words still those of the question it answers. Enter searches at once; a search is kept among the recent ones only when someone settles on it (Enter, a recent search repeated, a result opened). Words brought from the palette are searched at once and kept. Recent searches show before anything is asked, and repeating one turns its modifiers back into chips.

Messages and Files tabs: Files asks the same question with has:file (unless a filter already asks for files) and shows one row per file, marked with the words searched for. Results are read through usePagedList, 30 at a time, with LoadMore at the end instead of Previous and Next pages.

Since Q07 the results are read again in place, from the top as far as they had been read, when changedContent advances for a channel among them, leaving a read in flight to finish first and asking once more if it began before the change. Results are still a copy: after a resync beyond the event log they are stale until asked again.
inConversation opens it on the conversation it was asked from, as an In chip, from the header's menu (UX-23), without adding a recent search.

entries.plain: Lists what is new for you, everything unread, mentions or replies in threads you follow, grouped by conversation, one line each. New ones appear while it is open, and more load as you scroll.
entries.summary: Lists unread messages, mentions and followed-thread replies in groups, as a live, scroll-to-load list with coalesced refreshes.
details: Tabs All, Mentions and Threads (UX-52) ask the server's unread, mentions and threads modes; Threads shows only where the ready snapshot says activityThreads. Each tab is its own PagedList. Mention counts, edits and retention in conversations it shows, and in All and Threads each followed thread's lastSeq (All also each conversation's newest seq), signal that it may be out of date (UX-08).
A 250 ms coalesced refresh merges bursts, reads again as far as was shown and keeps existing content meanwhile.

groupActivity puts rows under one heading per conversation (per thread in Threads), in the order each group's newest came, named like "#design, 3 new"; a one-to-one DM's group is "Direct message" since its rows name the person. A row is one line (author, in a thread, time, the start of the text from notificationBody) and opens the message; Mark read reads a conversation, or a thread through markThreadRead's through, up to that row, and Save toggles saved. Mark all read reads every conversation and followed thread to its newest, and any listed reply in a thread not followed. Focus moves to the next row when the one holding it leaves.

entries.plain: A side panel listing your direct messages, newest first, with what is unread, so a conversation with someone is two taps away on a phone.
entries.summary: Lists the account's direct and group conversations from live state as a side panel, with unread, mention, draft and muted marks.
details: Opened by DMs in the phone's bottom bar, and at #/c/<channel>/p/dms. Like every side panel it loads on first use in LazyPanel, takes focus on its heading through usePanelFocus, and below 1024 px covers the conversation.

The list is the sidebar's own: conversations of type dm or group_dm this account is in and that are not archived, newest first by channelLastSeq. It comes from the workspace's live state, so it keeps itself current with nothing to load once the workspace has arrived; before then it shows ListStatus's stand-in rows.

Each row is a button at least 48 px tall with the first other person's avatar and presence, the conversation's name, and Draft, Muted, a red mention count or an Unread dot; the one open is marked. Choosing one opens it, which closes the panel. The header has Friends (with a dot for requests waiting) and New message, which a guest does not get.

Empty, it says how to start one and offers New message; a guest is told direct messages are for members. While the connection is down a line says the list may be out of date, and what this device knows stays listed.

entries.plain: Shows the messages you scheduled to send later, including failed ones, and lets you edit, reschedule or cancel them.
entries.summary: Shows queued, held and failed schedules and lets the author resolve them.
details: Loads server-owned schedules and presents future delivery times, status and attachment context.

Supports editing/rescheduling, cancelling and returning words to the appropriate draft. Server scheduling uses request identity, while the client preserves actionable refusal state and reads the queue again after an edit it could not confirm.
It reads the queue again whenever scheduledChanges moves: the server's private scheduled event, or a new connection. Only a server without scheduledEvents is still asked every 15 seconds (UX-08).

entries.plain: Shows attached files as cards, loads image previews as they scroll into view, and opens them full size.
entries.summary: Displays file cards, lazy authenticated image previews and full-size lightboxes.
details: Image loading begins near the viewport using IntersectionObserver, then retains/releases the shared FileCache resource. Large or non-image files use cards and scoped download URLs instead of eager inline transfer.

A resource is bound to the active client/file and can show loading, failure, retry or invalidated state. N10 cache notices make open previews become unavailable when their owner message/thread is removed.

Pending attachments use temporary local previews; lightboxes share the modal focus layer. The UI distinguishes a failed download from successful handoff rather than claiming the browser/OS completed it.
The full-size viewer itself is Lightbox.tsx, loaded on first use behind an error boundary; this file keeps the shared useFileResource and saveUrl it reads through.

entries.plain: The full-size view of a picture, with Save and Close, loaded the first time a picture is opened.
entries.summary: Shows one image full size over the conversation through the shared file resource.
details: Reads the image through Attachments' useFileResource, so loading, failure, retry and a file taken away behave as in inline previews; a picture that will not decode says so and can still be saved.
Kept out of the entry every visit downloads: Attachments' Lightbox loads it on first use, shows nothing new while it loads, and says the viewer could not load if its chunk fails.

entries.plain: The Send later choices beside the message box: a few times from now, or any date and time.
entries.summary: Offers scheduling presets and a custom local time, loaded when the composer's clock is first pressed.
details: The whole popover mounts at once, so Popover measures and places it with its real height; the custom time lives here and is cleared when it closes.
The button names the time chosen before it is scheduled. Composer still owns the request, its recovery record and what it says once the server confirms.

entries.plain: Turns message formatting like bold, code, quotes, mentions and links into what you see, and reveals where a link really goes.
entries.summary: Renders the supported Slack-style message syntax into React elements.
details: Handles fenced and inline code, bold/italic/strike, quotes, user/channel references and ordinary or labelled HTTP links without interpreting message text as arbitrary HTML.

Resolves mentions against supplied users/channels, with the same labels the composer shows (mentionDocument), and opens a message link in-place only when it belongs to a known address of this workspace.
A labelled link that looks like a different host exposes the actual destination. Code/quote edge trimming avoids artificial blank lines around block elements.

entries.plain: The emoji picker, laid out like Slack's: the ones you use most, every emoji by section, a search, and a skin tone choice.
entries.summary: Lets someone find any emoji by section, search or keyboard, in their skin tone.
details: Marks along the top jump to Frequently used and Slack's eight sections; the grid has nine emoji to a row under sticky section titles. The footer names the emoji under the pointer or the arrows with its :shortcode:, and holds the skin tone choice.

Focus stays in the search box, a combobox, and a screen reader follows the choice through aria-activedescendant. Up and Down move a row, into the next section where one ends; Left and Right move one emoji once the arrows are in the grid or nothing is typed; Enter picks.

Sections out of view are held open at their exact height and drawn when scrolling, a jump or the arrows come near, so opening it does not make all 1,870 emoji. Each section draws again only when the choice moves in or out of it or the tone changes.
Section marks are Its Hover's and Lucide's drawings; THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md credits them.

entries.plain: The formatting buttons and shortcuts, such as bold and italic, shared by the message box and the edit box, plus the length limit.
entries.summary: Shares formatting transformations, shortcuts and message length limits.
details: formatText wraps or inserts syntax and returns the corresponding selection so composer/editor behavior stays consistent.
The toolbar supplies supported formatting and preview affordances; formattingShortcut and MESSAGE_LIMIT keep keyboard handling and validation aligned.

Its emoji button opens the same EmojiPicker the reactions use, loaded on first use, with a loading line meanwhile and a message if it cannot load. Escape, its own button or a press anywhere outside it closes it, and a press outside leaves focus where it landed.

entries.plain: Where you pick an emoji to react to a message with, hanging off the message, or as its own window on a touchscreen.
entries.summary: Places the shared emoji picker beside a message, or in a dialog on touch.
details: Shows EmojiPicker in a Popover anchored to the message with a pointer, and in a Dialog on a touchscreen, and closes as the reaction is sent.
Touch users tap before opening the software keyboard, allowing the picker to show choices without the keyboard immediately covering them.

Kept out of the entry every visit downloads: MessageItem loads it the first time someone asks for more than the toolbar's three reactions, shows nothing new while it loads, and says the picker could not load if its chunk fails.

entries.plain: The line above a reply showing who wrote the message it answers and how that message began, as Discord draws it.
entries.summary: Renders an inline reply's quote and leads back to the original.
details: A curved line runs from the reply's avatar to the original author's small avatar, name and a one-line excerpt with mentions shown as names and formatting marks left out.

Clicking it is handled by the message row: an original on screen is scrolled to and briefly lit, and one that is not is opened by the same jump search and links use. A deleted original says so and opens nothing.

entries.plain: The sidebar with your workspaces, starred conversations, channels, direct messages, unread marks and account menu.
entries.summary: Combines workspace switching, conversation navigation, unread context and account actions.
details: A compact workspace rail and workspace menu expose remembered workspaces without presenting saved tokens to the visible navigation.
Channel and DM rows show unread/muted/activity state and choose destinations supplied by the workspace screen. Admin actions appear only where the current account can use them.
Snooze controls compute actual resume times and use the client's latest-choice behavior. Menu grouping saves vertical space so short windows retain room for conversations.

A guest's sidebar leaves out Friends, Scheduled, New channel and direct messages, says Guest under the name, and offers Create an account in place of invites and account settings. Once the guest has posted, KeepAccountOffer sits above the account panel (UX-44).

A channel's row ends with Discord's two buttons while it is pointed at, holds the keyboard, or is open: invite and settings. Invite on a public channel opens the workspace's invite, since everyone in the workspace is in every public channel, and only for someone who may invite; on a private one it is Add people, which opens the channel's Members tab, for someone channelPermissions lets invite. The gear opens the channel's details, opening the channel first if it is not the one on screen. The buttons sit beside the row's button, not in it, and on a touchscreen show on the open channel only.

HostingStatus is this computer's hosting, under the workspace's name and its connection line (UX-25): a dot for live, starting or stopping, or trouble, what it is doing or what is wrong, and Manage (named Manage hosting for a screen reader). A warning is an alert. It replaced a bar along the bottom of the window, and leaves out the workspace's name when the hosted workspace is the one on screen. The storage gate's waiting screen shows it too.

AccountMenu is exported for the phone's bottom bar, which opens the same menu from its own You button by passing trigger (its label, class and content); the menu then rises as a sheet on a touch phone. The sidebar's own trigger is unchanged.

Starred (UX-20) sits above Channels once something is starred, and goes when nothing is. A starred channel or direct message moves out of its usual section, as in Slack, and keeps its unread, mention, draft and muted marks. Starred lists by name, channels and people together, so a row stays where it was put rather than moving each time a message arrives. It folds away like Channels and Direct messages and is remembered on this device with them. An archived channel leaves it with its star kept, and comes back to it if the channel is brought back.

Every conversation's row ends with More (⋯), after invite and settings on a channel's: Star or Unstar, offered only where the server keeps stars, and Mute or Unmute, each named by what it does now. A right-click on the row, or the keyboard's menu key, opens the same menu. The row's buttons stay shown while the menu is open (data-menu-open), so the menu has a place to sit and focus a place to come back to. A row starred or unstarred from its own menu changes section, and focus follows it to its More button there, or to the header of a folded section it went into.
The workspace menu offers Workspace settings to the owner and admins, after People and Apps; members and guests do not see it (UX-60).

entries.plain: On a phone, a bar along the bottom of the screen with Home, DMs, Activity and You, so the places people look for most are in sight. It also lets a swipe in from the left edge open the list of channels, and keeps the screen clear of the on-screen keyboard.
entries.summary: The phone's bottom navigation bar, the edge swipe that opens the drawer, and the on-screen keyboard handling, for the web client.
details: The bar shows at the width half of theme.css's drawer query (760 px and narrower), so on a phone held upright; on its side a phone keeps the drawer alone, since height is what it lacks there. The web client only: the desktop app's window is never a phone. It is a nav named Main navigation, each place a button 56 px tall with an icon and its label, the one you are in marked with aria-current.

Home goes back to the conversation from a panel, and from the conversation opens the drawer with every channel, as a tab bar's current tab goes to its top. DMs opens the Direct messages panel and Activity the Activity panel; both cover the conversation and stop above the bar, so moving between them is one tap. You opens the sidebar's AccountMenu from its own button, as a sheet on a touch phone. A guest has no DMs, so the bar has three places.

Badges count what waits elsewhere, as the drawer's button does: the conversation on screen and muted ones do not count. Home has a dot for unread channels, DMs a red count of unread conversations, Activity a red count of mentions or a dot for unread replies in followed threads. Each is also said in words, as the button's description.

The bar is inert under the open drawer, which covers it. useEdgeSwipe opens the drawer while theme.css's drawer query matches and no dialog is open; useOnScreenKeyboard runs on every size, so the layout follows the keyboard on a phone on its side too.
With the drawer closed, the sidebar's heading, the workspace's name, is hidden with it, so a visually hidden copy stays the page's h1, in a top-level header (the page's banner).

entries.plain: The Ctrl+K box for jumping to a channel, a direct message or a person.
entries.summary: Provides Ctrl+K navigation to channels, DMs and people.
details: Builds labelled suggestion rows and keeps text-field focus with useListbox; IME Enter stays text input.
Existing conversations navigate directly, while a person without a DM starts one and shows pending/failure state. This is a navigation convenience over the server-authorized openDm operation.
It is kept out of the entry every visit downloads and fetched as soon as the workspace opens; see WorkspaceScreen.

entries.plain: The side panel listing who is in a conversation, grouped by who is online.
entries.summary: Shows the active conversation's people grouped by online presence.
details: DMs use their known participant IDs; channels fetch membership when opened and ignore results after disposal.
Active users are sorted by name, grouped online/offline and linked to profiles. Shared loading and focus helpers make failure/retry and dismissal consistent.
A channel's list is asked for again, in place, when someone joins or leaves (memberChanges).

entries.plain: The channel settings window for its topic and description, its members and managers, and your notifications for it.
entries.summary: Edits channel details and manages membership, managers and notification choices.
details: Presents topic/description and member controls under shared channel permission rules; the server remains responsible for enforcement.
Updates, inviting/removing members, changing managers and leaving map API refusals into readable actions. Channel notification writes expose retry rather than silently abandoning a refused choice.
Opens on About, or on Members (initialTab) when Add people on a private channel's row in the sidebar opens it.
The Notifications tab's not-saved notice speaks for the notify level and muting only. A star that was not saved says so where it was chosen.

entries.plain: Windows for making and browsing channels, starting a direct message and turning a guest into an account.
entries.summary: Groups channel creation/browsing, new conversations and guest account forms.
details: NewChannelDialog creates public/private channels; BrowseChannelsDialog lists and joins available channels; NewDmDialog chooses participants and opens a direct/group conversation.

These occasional forms are lazy-loaded by the workspace screen rather than required for every returning conversation view. Invite people moved to InviteDialog.tsx, so its QR encoder loads with it alone.

GuestAccountDialog keeps a guest's identity as an account; the new session token reopens the workspace as the same person. Its Username and Password are TextFields checked on submit with the server's rules (2 to 32 lowercase letters, digits, . _ or -, and at least 8 characters): the button is never off until filled in, each problem is said under its field, the first gets focus, and a taken username comes back under the username.

entries.plain: The Invite people window. It opens with a link ready to copy, a QR code for phones, and a way to make a link that lasts longer or lets fewer people in.
entries.summary: Invite people: a link ready on opening, inline length and use limits, QR code, and the list of codes (UX-43).
details: On opening it shows the newest invite this person made that still works like a new one, or makes one for seven days and any number of people, so there is no generate step and opening it again does not mint another code.

Change makes a new link from Expires after and Number of uses choices. Copy link confirms with a toast as well as on the button; the QR code is left out when the only address reaches this computer alone.
It lists invites with their status and lets the creator or an administrator revoke one after a confirmation. Clipboard outcome and readable server refusal state are preserved.

With welcome it is the step that ends founding a workspace (UX-42): titled Invite your people, it leaves out the list, ends with Done, and says when the link only works on its own network, pointing a desktop host to Manage, under the workspace's name, to share the workspace on the internet.

entries.plain: Draws a QR code for a link on this device, dark on white in either theme, so a phone camera can open it.
entries.summary: Renders a QR code as one SVG path with a quiet zone, using the uqr encoder.
details: Encodes with error correction level M, which survives about 15 percent of the code being smudged or covered, and keeps the four-module quiet zone scanners need.
Nothing leaves the device: the encoder runs in the page, never through a service.

entries.plain: Shows someone's profile with a way to message them, and lets you edit your own name and status.
entries.summary: Displays a person's profile and provides the shared self-profile editor.
details: ProfileForm updates the current user's name and status through Api. Another person's profile can start/open a direct message.
Since Q11 a press on Message is dropped once the card closes or shows someone else, so a late answer neither navigates nor changes the card.

Your own form offers Clear after (30 minutes, 1 hour, Today, This week, Don't clear) once there is a status; a preset picks its usual length, and a status saved again keeps the end it was set with. Someone else's card says until when their status lasts (UX-61).

entries.plain: Lists your friends in the workspace and lets you send, accept or remove friend requests.
entries.summary: Lists contacts and friend-request actions within the workspace.
details: FriendActions requests, accepts or removes a relationship through Api and displays current request state.
The list resolves workspace people and supports opening their profiles or conversations; relationship state belongs to the server-backed replica.

entries.plain: The Account settings page, with sections for your profile, notifications, appearance, calls, security, devices and storage, a search that goes straight to a setting, and a quiet "Saved" when a choice is kept.
entries.summary: A full-window page of account, device and presentation settings in routable sections.
details: Section keyboard navigation and route callbacks connect profile, notifications, appearance, composing, calls, security, devices and storage to Back/Forward history.

A page over the whole window rather than a box in it (UX-60), still built on Modal for focus, Escape and the inert page behind. In the desktop app it starts under the 40 px title bar so the window controls stay usable. On the left, on the sidebar's colour, are its name, whose account it is, a search field and the sections; on the right the open section is the only part that scrolls, as a page does, and opens at its start. On a phone the sections are a strip that brings the chosen one to its middle.

The search lists matching settings from settingsSearch in place of the sections. Enter or a click opens the setting's section, scrolls the setting to the middle, focuses its control (or its heading) and marks it briefly for anyone who sees no focus ring. Escape in a filled search clears it; the next one closes the page.

Choices that save themselves report through savedNote, and the section's title row says "Saved" for two seconds in a polite live region that is always present, so it is read out without competing with the section's own status messages.
Uses shared preference stores for notification preview, Enter behavior, appearance and join-muted choice. Calls includes a local microphone check and N04 retry for unreadable call preferences.
Security and Devices change passwords, list/revoke sessions and sign out through the server; Storage displays server usage. Confirmation identifies destructive session changes.
The Q03 and Q04 repairs live in the underlying helpers; this dialog only shows their state, including Try again for a composer preference that could not be read.

entries.plain: The Workspace settings page, where the workspace's owner and admins rename it and choose who may join, with a quiet "Saved" when a choice is kept.
entries.summary: A full-window page for the workspace's own name and join policy, for its owner and admins (UX-60).
details: Built like Account settings: a page over the whole window on Modal, its sections (General, Who can join) on the left as tabs and the open one on the right. It loads on first use, so it adds nothing to the entry chunk.

General has the workspace's name in a TextField with Save. Save is never disabled: sent empty or with a tab or line break, the field says what is wrong and takes the cursor; a server refusal lands under the field too. While nothing is typed, a rename made elsewhere replaces what the field shows.

Who can join is a radio group of the three policies, each with a plain explanation, saved the moment one is chosen through WorkspaceClient.setAccessPolicy. The title row says "Saved" for two seconds through savedNote. A failed change shows what the server has and says why.

While guests are allowed a line says that choosing either other rule signs every guest out. When guests have joined, leaving guest_allowed asks first with useConfirm, since signed-out guests have to join again.

When this desktop app hosts the workspace on screen (hostedHere), the page says that Open to all in Manage hosting chooses who can join for the public link, and that Manage hosting shows and changes the same setting while the link is open.
On a server without ReadySnapshot.workspaceSettings it shows the name, offers neither control, and says the workspace is changed where it is hosted.

entries.plain: Lets admins see everyone's account and change roles, deactivate people, reset passwords or hand over ownership.
entries.summary: Lets administrators inspect accounts and manage access under server role rules.
details: Loads all users, offers role/deactivation/invite-permission actions, password reset and ownership transfer where permitted.

PersonMenu consolidates row actions into one accessible menu. Confirmations and mapped refusal messages communicate lost access, protected ownership and equal-admin restrictions; hidden buttons are not treated as authorization.

entries.plain: Where bots and other connected apps are set up and managed, along with their slash commands and delivery status.
entries.summary: Manages bot apps, webhooks, commands, subscriptions and callback configuration.
details: Creates and removes integrations and exposes explicit credential replacement actions. Bot tokens shown once stay only in this UI session; rereadable secrets have reveal/copy controls.
Configures slash commands, event subscriptions and verified interactivity URLs; refreshes composer command hints when those change.
Delivery status distinguishes waiting, given-up and never-queued events and offers retry where supported.

It opens on templates (UX-63): Incoming webhook, Slash command and Post CI results, as tabs sharing one choice of app (a new one or an existing one) and channel, so a webhook made in one is ready in another. A webhook template makes the app and webhook in one click, fills its URL into the example and posts the example's message to the URL itself (postToWebhook). The command template adds the command, fills the app's signing secret into the example service (dotted out on screen, copied whole) and runs /command test in a chosen channel, showing the server's reason when the app fails.
OAuth, Socket Mode, ts and the link to the published integration contract are folded into How this differs from Slack.

Each app's Slash commands, Event subscriptions and Interactivity forms are fieldsets named by their legend, with small TextFields (Command, Request URL, Description). Their buttons are never off until filled in: sent empty, a form says what is missing under each field and focuses the first, and a request in flight is only aria-disabled. A refused event or interactivity address is said under the field. Saving the interactivity address works unchanged too, rechecking it, and says Saved and verified, or that buttons are off when it is empty.

entries.plain: Shows a page-by-page history of admin changes, written as readable sentences.
entries.summary: Shows paged administrator changes as readable audit sentences.
details: Looks up current names from stored IDs and defensively interprets details, so newer or partial records remain understandable.
Loads only when requested, pages through the server audit log and preserves keyboard focus when the final page removes a pagination control.
Renaming the workspace and changing who can join read as sentences too, with the old and new name, or the new rule in plain words; an entry made by the desktop app's host names the host.

entries.plain: In the desktop app, starts and stops the workspace you host and handles its folder, backups, who may join and outside access.
entries.summary: Controls desktop hosting, workspace folders, backup/restore and public reachability.
details: The browser does not own a server; native Platform.hosting provides the operations this dialog presents. Existing workspace folders and new workspace names are separate start intents.
Presents running/stopped/startup status, port and rename controls, LAN and public-address choices, connector failure and launch recovery actions.
Lists hosted workspaces and backup schedules, supports backup/restore and explains a restored copy's pending apps, schedules, deliveries and sessions before activation.

N11/N12 fixes live in the desktop registry/controller: restored safety holds survive damaged metadata and cleanup ownership gates reopening. The dialog exposes those statuses; Q12 and Q13 closed the startup and queue gaps in the desktop main process, not in this dialog.

Who may join is two choices, Require an account to join and, under it, Require an invite link; clearing the first lets visitors join as guests. Before opening the choice travels with openToAll; while open it is applied with setAccessPolicy and shown as the workspace acknowledges it.

A running workspace is managed in tabs (UX-62): Overview (name with a Live pill, its network and public addresses with Copy and a QR code, who is connected, and Invite people, or Open it when another workspace is on screen), Share on the internet (plain words, then the public link card and the call relay), Backups (last backup, Back up now, the schedule) and Advanced (start-up, data folder, port). A tab shows only where this app can do what it holds. Stop hosting stays in the footer under every tab and stops without asking.

entries.plain: The hosting card that sets up a relay so calls work between people on different networks, and tests that it answers.
entries.summary: The Calls from other networks card in Manage hosting: no relay, Cloudflare, or another TURN server.
details: Shows the saved relay without its secret; a token or password left empty keeps the saved one for the same key or username. Save reaches calls that start afterwards.

Test asks the app for the relay servers a call would be given and runs probeRelay, saying whether the relay works, refused the password, or could not be reached. A refusal calls found out about since is shown as an alert.

entries.plain: Keeps the workspace's best address ready, so copying a link is instant and points somewhere others can reach.
entries.summary: Keeps known workspace addresses ready before the user copies a link.
details: Combines server-info, native hosting status and explicitly trusted aliases to choose a sharing address without awaiting a network request in the clipboard click handler.
Rechecks after reconnect, foreground return and periodically while open so temporary/public addresses can refresh. Context also tells Mrkdwn which workspace message links can navigate in-place.

entries.plain: A setup checklist that ticks itself off as you create a channel, invite someone, turn on notifications and join a huddle.
entries.summary: Shows setup steps that complete from actual workspace/account behavior.
details: Tracks creating a channel, inviting someone, enabling notifications and participating in a huddle, with account/workspace-local dismissal memory.
The checklist can disappear after completion or explicit dismissal. N04's screen wiring makes its huddle action use the preference-aware join operation.

entries.plain: A small card in a guest's sidebar, shown after their first message, offering to keep them as an account with their name, their messages and a place in private conversations.
entries.summary: Offers a guest the keep-account form once, after the server has accepted their first message.
details: A guest has posted once the replica holds a message of theirs: only the server's copy reaches a timeline or a thread, while one still sending or failed waits in pending. A guest who posted before the card existed is found the same way, and the first sighting is stored, so a reload offers it even where that message is not loaded.

Not now, or Keep this account, puts it away for that account on this device: stored per workspace and account like the setup checklist, and remembered by the page as well, so a save that fails does not bring it back before a reload. Storage that cannot be read means it is not offered at all, since an earlier Not now cannot be ruled out; the menus still have Create an account.

Keep this account opens the same form as Create an account in the menus. The card sits above the account panel, so the channel list does not move when it appears, and its width is contained, so its words never widen the sidebar; it takes no focus and makes no announcement, and focus inside it when it is put away goes to the account button. It goes as soon as the guest is a member.

entries.plain: A banner asking to turn on browser notifications, which waits two weeks before asking again if you pick Not now.
entries.summary: Requests browser notification permission from an intentional visible gesture.
details: Appears after sign-in rather than asking from an unrelated first click. Not now defers the banner for two weeks on this device.
An explicit browser denial remains quiet until site permission changes, and the native desktop notification adapter does not need this banner.
It sits in the workspace's one banner place and gives way to anything more pressing (UX-25). onShowing tells the workspace whether it is on show, so the Opening message… hint behind it waits.

entries.plain: Reads out new messages to screen reader users without moving focus, grouping bursts so they are not flooded.
entries.summary: Politely announces new visible messages without flooding a screen reader.
details: A single arrival includes a bounded excerpt; a burst groups count and up to a few sender names after a quiet period.
Announcements do not steal focus, and navigation clears old-conversation waiting messages so they are not announced in the new destination.

entries.plain: The button at the top of a conversation that starts a huddle, joins one in progress or shows you are in it.
entries.summary: Header control that starts a huddle, joins the running one, or says you are in it.
details: Names the action by the room's state (Start a huddle, Join the huddle (n), In huddle) and joins through the same preference-aware path as other entry points.

entries.plain: The parts of a conversation's header besides its name: the faces of who is in it, the menu with everything else, and the line that says how many messages are pinned.
entries.summary: Member faces and count, the conversation's ⋯ menu, and the pinned line under the header.
details: MemberStack shows up to three faces, people online first, and a count; it opens and closes the Members panel. A group message knows its people; a channel's are asked for, and asked again when memberChanges moves or the connection comes back. A phone shows one face.

ConversationMenu holds Pinned messages, Search in #name (search opened on this conversation), Star or Unstar ("channel", or "conversation" for people), Notification settings (the details' Notifications tab, only for a member) and the details. Star shows only for a member, on a server that keeps stars.

PinnedBar asks for one pin and the total, shows "3 pinned" with the newest pin's first words, and opens the Pinned panel; it asks again when changedContent moves, so a pin, an unpin or an edit shows at once. A server too old to count says only "Pinned".
The last answers are kept per client, so going back to a conversation shows its faces and pins at once instead of the header moving as they arrive.

entries.plain: One row in the place for banners under a conversation's header: what happened, and what can be done about it.
entries.summary: The banner row (alert or status) and its actions, for the workspace's one banner place (UX-25).
details: Banner takes a tone, its words and optional actions at its end. An alert is tinted and read out at once by a screen reader; a status is a quiet passing note.
BannerAction is a button whose words underline on hover, as a link would, such as Dismiss or Retry saving.
Which banner shows is WorkspaceScreen's choice, one at a time. App builds the one for sign-ins this device could not save, which the storage gate also shows while the workspace is not open yet.

entries.plain: The call bar showing who is in the huddle, who is speaking, each person's volume and anyone you cannot connect to.
entries.summary: Shows call presence, speaking rings and the header join/start control.
details: HuddleFace resolves participants and speaking state, while the compact bar hosts controls and a way to restore hidden video.

The list of who is there (Everyone in the huddle) gives each of the others a PersonVolume row. Someone muted for you is said to be, ahead of talking, with a crossed speaker on their face. The bar hands everyone's volume to HuddleAudio.
HuddleButton starts or joins through the shared call-preference store and provides meaningful error state. N04 makes this header path agree with Getting started about mute initialization.
Once a peer's connection has a diagnosed trouble, the bar says Can't connect to them and offers Why? See the call log.

entries.plain: The mute, camera, screen share and leave buttons, with menus to switch microphone, speaker or camera.
entries.summary: Provides shared microphone, camera, screen-share and leave actions.
details: Used by both the compact bar and fullscreen stage so the call actions stay available in either layout.
Stable accessible names plus aria-pressed describe toggles; captureFailure distinguishes a cancelled picker from a permission/device problem. A lost microphone exposes retry.

Beside Mute and Camera, a small arrow opens a menu of microphones and speakers, or cameras, with the chosen one ticked (menuitemradio) and a link to Voice & video settings. The menus are left out of the full-screen overlay, because menus open on the page beneath a fullscreen element.

In the desktop app, Share screen opens ScreenShareDialog rather than asking the browser; a browser shows its own picker, and stopping needs none. Whether the picker is open is one small store for the window: the bar's controls draw it, and the controls in full screen leave full screen first, since a dialog does not show over it and those controls go with it.

entries.plain: The desktop app's screen picker, like Discord's: tabs for windows and screens, a live picture of each, and the resolution and frame rate to share at.
entries.summary: Picks a window or screen to share, and how sharp and smooth, in the app rather than a system dialog.
details: Windows come first and none is chosen for you, since the window on top is usually Tandem itself; the Screens tab starts on the first screen, and a list with no window opens on it. Tiles are radio buttons in a radiogroup; a double click or Enter shares at once.

The last list shows at once where there has been one (platform.screenShare.sources with quick), then a fresh one, then again every 3 s while open, so pictures move and windows come and go; a chosen window that closes leaves Share with nothing to share. Only a first fresh list that fails with nothing shown says so, with Try again.

Share names the choice to the main process, then asks the huddle for a screen at the quality chosen (720p or 1080p; 15, 30 or 60 fps, kept on the device as screen-share-quality). A window that closed since it was listed, or a refusal from the system, is said in the dialog, which stays open; chosen here, even a plain refusal says sharing could not start.

entries.plain: Plays everyone's voice in a call through your chosen speaker at the volume you set, even with the video hidden.
entries.summary: Keeps each remote microphone playing independently of video layout.
details: Peer audio elements attach microphone streams even when the call has no camera or the video stage is hidden.
Playback refusal produces a recovery action; one user gesture retries blocked peers while already audible streams are left intact. This avoids duplicate audio from video elements.
Each peer's audio element plays through the speaker chosen in Voice & video settings.

Each person plays as loud as you chose. Up to 100% the element's own volume does it, so the usual path is untouched. Past 100% their stream goes through a Web Audio gain into a stream the same element plays, so the chosen speaker still applies. A second, muted element holds their stream meanwhile, since Chromium gives an audio graph silence from a call's stream that no element plays (measured: 0 without it).
A boost's graph that will not start without a gesture is reported like a refused play, so Turn on sound starts it.

entries.plain: One person's volume control in a call, with a mute just for you and a slider up to 200 percent.
entries.summary: One person's volume in a call: mute for you, and a slider from silent to 200%.
details: A toggle button (aria-pressed) mutes the person for you alone, and a range input in steps of 5 sets their volume, with a tick at 100% from a datalist and the percent beside it, or Off.
Moving the slider unmutes them, since it means wanting to hear them. Used in the bar's list of who is there and inside a stage tile.

entries.plain: The video area of a call, which lays out cameras and screen shares as large as the window allows.
entries.summary: Arranges cameras and shares into docked, gallery, presenting or spotlight views.
details: stageItems prioritizes screen shares then participants; bestFit tries column counts to find the largest 16:9 tiles for the actual container dimensions.
Video surfaces stay muted because HuddleAudio owns voices. Local self-video and remote camera/share streams display without opening a second media capture.
Resize observation updates layout, and accessible tiles/actions expose focus, fullscreen and share controls. Lazy loading keeps the stage out of initial conversation downloads until needed.

Another person's tile, in the gallery or the main view, has a volume button beside Pin. Its PersonVolume opens inside the tile rather than as a popover, because popovers portal to the page beneath a fullscreen element. A tile says when its person is muted for you.

entries.plain: Lets you hear and see how your microphone sounds before a huddle, without sending anything to anyone.
entries.summary: Lets the user test local microphone level before joining a huddle.
details: Opens the chosen microphone with the chosen processing through client-core's testMicrophone, the strong noise filter included, so what plays back is what a call would send; if the filter cannot start it says the browser's own suppression is standing in. It shows the microphone's name and level, and opens it again when the choice changes; autoStart listens at once, as the first-huddle question does. An optional playback sends the voice to the chosen speaker.
Nothing is sent to peers or the server. Stopping the check or closing settings stops the captured tracks.

entries.plain: The Voice & video settings, where you pick devices, set noise suppression and test your microphone, speaker and camera.
entries.summary: The Voice & video section of Account settings: devices, processing and tests.
details: Microphone, speaker (where setSinkId exists) and camera pickers with the system default first; a chosen device that is unplugged stays listed as such. Changes apply to a huddle in progress through chooseDevices and are kept for every workspace on this device.

Noise suppression as Strong, Standard or Off (Discord's choice; Strong unless chosen otherwise, and Off for anyone who had turned suppression off), echo cancellation and automatic volume switches, a microphone test with playback, a two-tone speaker test, a mirrored camera preview, and join-muted. When the browser keeps device names back it offers to ask for the microphone once.
On the Account settings page it leaves out its own heading (titled={false}), since the page already names the section, and reports kept device and join-muted choices through savedNote.

entries.plain: Asks once, before your first huddle, which microphone and camera to use when you have more than one.
entries.summary: Asks once, before a first huddle, which microphone and camera to use.
details: callPreferences.joinHuddle asks when this device has not been asked (devicesChecked), nothing is chosen, and the browser lists more than one microphone or camera; a browser that keeps names back lists none, so it is asked on the first join after it gives them. Choosing a microphone or camera in settings counts as an answer.

The dialog, loaded on first use from WorkspaceScreen, listens through MicrophoneCheck and shows the camera through CameraPreview at once. Join huddle keeps the choice and joins with it; Cancel, or the workspace closing, joins nothing and asks again next time. Only a dialog that went without an answer calls the waiting join off.

entries.plain: Shows the full diagnostics report, call logs included, so you can read it before copying or saving it.
entries.summary: Shows the complete diagnostics report before copying or downloading it.
details: Reads server-info and optional owner/admin operating status, recording a readable failure when either is unavailable.
The person can inspect the report and choose copy or local text-file save; the dialog does not send diagnostics to another service.
The report includes this device's call log and, for the owner and admins, the server's call log, with people named by handle. Opened from a call that cannot connect, it starts at the call log.

entries.plain: A searchable list of keyboard shortcuts that follows your Enter to send setting.
entries.summary: Lists and filters keyboard shortcuts using the current composing preference.
details: Writing-key descriptions change with Enter-to-send so the help reflects active behavior.
A query matches words across keys and explanations, exposing navigation, message, formatting and call shortcuts without requiring the reader to memorize them.
Each key is drawn with the shared Kbd keycap.

entries.plain: Draws each person's colored initials and the dot that shows whether they are online.
entries.summary: Draws consistent initials avatars and presence indicators without image downloads.
details: Avatar uses the account's deterministic hue and display-name initials; missing users receive a fallback.
PresenceDot and AvatarWithPresence draw online state with a ring matching the parent surface, keeping the same visual rule across rows and calls.

entries.plain: The app's set of small icons and its logo, drawn directly so nothing extra has to download. Six of them move when you point at their button.
entries.summary: Provides the application's small inline SVG icon vocabulary and brand mark.
details: IconName maps to shared vector paths, stroke/size conventions and accessible usage supplied by parent controls.
Inline vectors avoid an icon font, extra network fetch and a large icon runtime dependency while keeping common controls visually consistent.

Six icons (smile, reply, thread, bookmark, edit and the three dots) are redrawn after Its Hover's and kept as named parts. Such an icon carries data-icon and each path data-part, and every part has a path length of 1, so the stylesheet can move or draw one part without a motion library in the bundle.
home (a house) and messages (two speech bubbles) are the phone's bottom bar's Home and DMs.
star (five points) is Star and Unstar in a conversation's menus.

entries.plain: The app's standard buttons, in main, secondary, danger and quiet styles.
entries.summary: Centralizes primary, secondary, danger and quiet action styling.
details: buttonClass lets existing native buttons reuse variants; Button forwards native attributes and ref.
Preserves native button semantics, including form submission unless type=button is explicitly chosen.

entries.plain: A button that shows only an icon. It cannot be made without a name, which a screen reader says and which appears as its hint.
entries.summary: The shared icon-only button: a required label used as accessible name and tooltip.
details: The label prop is required by its type and becomes both aria-label and the Tooltip's text; keys adds a shortcut to the tooltip. It takes an Icon name or other non-text children.
Two sizes: regular is 32 px (size-8) for dialogs, panels and headers, small is 24 px (size-6), the smallest target axe's target-size rule accepts. round draws a circle for one on a chip.

Unlike Button it defaults to type=button, since an icon rarely sends a form. It forwards its ref through Tooltip's ref merge and passes aria-pressed, aria-expanded and aria-haspopup through, tinting while pressed or expanded.

entries.plain: A text box with its name above it and, under it, a line on what to enter or what is wrong. It also holds the one set of styles every text box uses.
entries.summary: Labelled input with hint and error wiring, and the single source of field classes.
details: TextField draws a visible label tied by htmlFor, then the input, then an error (role=alert, with an icon) and a hint. aria-describedby lists the error first, then the hint, then any the caller passes; aria-invalid is set only while there is an error. Its ref reaches the input, so a form checked on submit can put the cursor in the first field with a problem.

inputClass(size, extra) returns the classes for small (a row of fields in a card), regular (dialogs and settings) and large (the sign-in card, with field-spot). Each size is a whole set, because two utilities for one property are settled by Tailwind's order rather than the class list's. aria-invalid:border-alert turns any of them red.
inputCls is the regular size, for an input, textarea or select still drawn by hand; it used to live in Dialog.tsx, with a second copy in JoinScreen.

entries.plain: Draws one keyboard key as a small keycap, as the shortcuts list shows them.
entries.summary: The shared keycap style for a key.
details: A kbd element with a raised face and a deeper lower edge; a shortcut of several keys is several side by side. It passes its props through and adds any classes given.
Keyboard shortcuts uses it. The plain shortcut hints in the quick switcher, the sidebar's Jump to button and a tooltip's bubble keep their own quieter styles.

entries.plain: The layer under every dialog, menu and full-size image, which keeps the keyboard inside the top one and returns focus on close.
entries.summary: Owns the shared stack of modal portals and keyboard/focus isolation.
details: Tracks the active layer, makes the page and older portals inert, and permits only the top layer to handle Escape, outside dismissal and tab containment.

Focus restoration follows connected usable openers and fallback owners even if an underlying dialog was removed. Layout registration accounts for child autoFocus occurring before portal ownership is fully installed.
Central ownership avoids competing independent focus traps for dialogs, menus and lightboxes.

A dialog's scrolling region (.dialog-scroll, or .settings-scroll on the Account settings page) is a part of it, so keys pressed elsewhere in it would scroll nothing. Page Up and Page Down from outside the region, and the arrow, Home and End keys from the dialog element itself, scroll the region. Text areas, selects and modified keys are left alone.

A dialog, menu or popover leaves as it came. When it closes, a copy of it, inert, hidden from screen readers and stripped of ids, names and roles, is put where it was and plays the reverse of its opening animation, then removes itself. One closed while still opening, as a loading placeholder is, leaves nothing, and neither does anything when less motion is asked for.

entries.plain: The standard dialog frame. Its title and close button stay in sight while what is under them scrolls.
entries.summary: Adds standard dialog structure and one scrolling region on top of Modal.
details: Supplies a titled surface, accessible description relationship, close affordance and configurable width.

The title row is fixed and the content scrolls in DialogScroll. A dialog that sets ownScroll places that region itself, between the parts it keeps in sight: a search field, the list of settings sections, or the buttons that finish a form.

The scrolling content takes its width from a container around the scroller, so a scrollbar appearing does not shift it, and it fades at an edge only while there is more to scroll to there. Both are stylesheet rules, with a plain edge where scroll timelines are unsupported.

entries.plain: A small panel that opens beside the button that opened it, such as the choices for Send later.
entries.summary: A small panel anchored to the control that opened it, such as Send later's choices.
details: Built on the modal layer like Menu: Escape or a press outside closes it, the page beneath waits, and focus returns to the control. It sits above the control, or below when there is no room, and follows it as the page scrolls.
side: "below" asks for the other way round, for a control at the top of what it changes, such as search's Date filter (UX-51).

entries.plain: The compact menu used for message and workspace actions, which works by keyboard as well as by mouse.
entries.summary: Provides one accessible compact menu for row and workspace actions.
details: Built on the modal layer, with arrow navigation, Enter selection, Escape/outside dismissal and focus return to the trigger.
Repositions with scrolling instead of abandoning an action when a live timeline shifts. Destructive and disabled items keep consistent presentation.
It grows from the corner nearest its trigger, which depends on whether it opened below or above it, and a phone's sheet rises from the bottom edge.
Ticked items are menuitemradio, one of a set, unless the menu is multiple: then each is a menuitemcheckbox, as search's From and Has filters are (UX-51).

entries.plain: The small hint that appears over a button when you point at it or reach it with the keyboard.
entries.summary: Explains compact controls without taking focus or blocking the page.
details: Hover opens after a short delay; keyboard focus opens immediately; Escape dismisses the hint. The floating portal follows its trigger and flips when needed.
Composes event handlers, accessible descriptions and refs, including React ref-cleanup behavior, so decorating a control does not replace its own lifetime contract.
The first hint waits 400 ms. Once one is showing, or has just gone, the next waits only 80 ms and slides over from where the last one was instead of growing in again. Hiding is immediate.

The floating text itself is TooltipBubble, out of the first download: loadTooltipBubble fetches it as the workspace opens or a hint is first wanted, and a hint opened before it arrives is drawn once it has.

entries.plain: Draws a hint's text beside its button and keeps it there as the page scrolls. It downloads in the background, so the app opens a little faster.
entries.summary: An open tooltip's floating text: placement, follow-on slide, Escape and window blur.
details: Placed in a portal on the trigger's dialog, main, nav or aside, or the fullscreen element holding it; flips sides when the preferred one does not fit, and follows its trigger on scroll, resize and every frame.

Split from Tooltip to make room for slice 7's status that clears itself, when the desktop entry stood at 499.2 kB of a 500 kB limit (since raised to 700 kB by #301): about 2.9 kB less for every first download.

entries.plain: Asks you to confirm before something that cannot be undone, and only goes ahead if you pick the named action.
entries.summary: Asks named questions for irreversible user actions and returns a boolean answer.
details: ConfirmProvider and useConfirm expose a promise resolved true only by the explicitly named action; cancellation, closing and Escape resolve false.
A destructive question begins on Cancel and can explain the consequence. Callers act on the answer rather than inferring permission from dismissal.

entries.plain: The small notices that say whether something worked, where failures stay until you dismiss them and may offer Retry or Undo.
entries.summary: Reports operation outcomes without interrupting current input.
details: Success notices clear after a reading interval, while failures remain for acknowledgement and can offer an operation-specific retry or undo.
A bounded stack pauses countdowns during hover/focus and preserves a nearby focus destination when a notice is removed. Notices never make the workspace inert.

A notice rises in out of a slight blur. One dismissed by pointer or by its timer fades as its row folds away, so the notices after it slide up; one closed from the keyboard goes at once, so focus can move to its neighbour.

entries.plain: Small pieces that make changes visible: a count that pops in and rolls when it changes, words or an icon that swap in place, and a panel that steps in from the side.
entries.summary: Shared change-driven motion: badges, in-place swaps and stepped panels.
details: useChanges counts how often a value has changed since the component was first drawn, so what was already on screen when it opened stays still and only later changes move.

CountBadge is drawn as nothing at zero and pops in when it appears; its number rolls up when it changes. Swap regrows an icon, or raises words, out of a blur when what it shows changes. stepIn brings a new page in from the side it is on.
All of it follows the motion tokens in theme.css, and none of it plays for anyone who asked for less motion.

entries.plain: Gives every list the same look while it is loading, refreshing, empty or offering to try again.
entries.summary: Keeps loading, refresh, empty and retry state consistent across lists.
details: Before first content it renders varied stand-in rows; later refreshes keep the current list and show a status line.

A stable live region and layout cleanup preserve focus when a Retry/empty-state action is replaced by results. This is a shared usability primitive rather than each panel inventing its own state layout.

entries.plain: The end of a long list. It loads the next part as you scroll near it, and is also a Show more button for keyboards.
entries.summary: End-of-list control that loads the next page when it comes into view (UX-08).
details: An IntersectionObserver rooted in the panel's scroller asks for the next page a little before the end is visible, and is made again after each page, so a short list keeps filling until it fills the panel or ends.
It stays one button while loading (aria-disabled, not disabled) so focus is not lost, says when more could not load with Try again, and hands focus to its own wrapper when the list ends.

entries.plain: Catches a part of the screen that breaks and offers to retry it, without losing your connection or what you typed.
entries.summary: Contains a broken React view while preserving the workspace connection and typed work.
details: Catches render failures and supplies recoverable fallback controls at the relevant boundary.
Dismissal can retry the same tree without automatically reloading the whole app, allowing the live client and unsent state outside that boundary to remain owned.

entries.plain: Shows a loading message while a panel or dialog downloads on first use, and offers to close or reload if that fails.
entries.summary: Wraps on-demand panels and dialogs with loading and failed-chunk recovery.
details: Suspense announces what is loading and retains a way to close the pending view.
An ErrorBoundary confines a failed download to that view and provides close/reload actions, allowing the rest of the workspace to remain usable.

entries.plain: A page for people building Tandem that shows every shared control in its states, in the dark and the light theme. Only the development version has it.
entries.summary: Development-only gallery of the UI primitives in Onyx and White, the reference for review.
details: apps/web/src/main.tsx imports it, through the package's ./gallery export, only when import.meta.env.DEV is true and the address is #/gallery, #/gallery/onyx or #/gallery/white. A build replaces that condition with false and drops the import, so neither the web build nor the desktop renderer contains it.

A theme belongs to the whole document, menus and tooltips included, so #/gallery shows each theme in an iframe of its own (#/gallery/onyx and #/gallery/white), and each sets data-theme on its own document. A framed sheet tells the page its height by postMessage, checked against the page's origin, so the page scrolls rather than the frames.

Sections show Button's variants and disabled and waiting states, IconButton's sizes and pressed, disabled and round forms, TextField with hint, error and disabled at each size, a form checked on submit (also inside a Dialog), Kbd, Tooltip, Menu, Popover, Toast and ListStatus's loading, refreshing, failed and empty states. Hover and focus are seen by pointing and tabbing.

flows.title: Sending a message
flows.summary: Different parts of Tandem look after what you type, the copy saved on your device and the message on the server. Sending passes the message along with a one-time code and waits for a confirmation, rather than just emptying the message box.

steps.title: Type and keep a draft
steps.description: The message box shows your words as you type them. The app saves the draft a moment after you pause, and right away when you switch conversations or close the app normally. A thread reply has its own draft, separate from the channel's.
steps.detail: Composer updates local text immediately, debounces client.setDraft for ordinary typing, and captures current text before navigation or normal close. Thread replies use their own draft key.

steps.title: Show the message right away
steps.description: The message shows up in the conversation right away, marked as sending, with previews of any attached files. The app gives it a random one-time code so it can recognise it later. If 50 messages are already waiting to send, the app refuses this one and keeps your draft.
steps.detail: WorkspaceClient validates admission, generates a random nonce, appends PendingMessage and creates local attachment previews. The 50-send limit refuses extra work while keeping the draft.

steps.title: Save it on the device before clearing the draft
steps.description: The message joins the messages waiting to send, saved on the device, and only then does the app clear the saved draft. The app counts the message as safe once it is saved on the device or delivered. If saving fails, the app keeps what it needs to try again or to give your words back.
steps.detail: DraftPersistence merges the outbox before clearing the corresponding saved draft. localWork settles the nonce after storage or delivery evidence; failures retain retry/recovery state.

steps.title: Upload files and post
steps.description: The app uploads any attached files, then sends the message to the server. If it has to try again, it does not upload the same files twice and sends exactly the same message. Upload progress shows on the message marked as sending.
steps.detail: deliver uploads chosen files, caches successful upload IDs for a retry and posts the exact message request. Progress belongs to the pending row.

steps.title: Swap in the confirmed message
steps.description: The server confirms the message, either in its answer or over the live connection. The app replaces the sending copy with the server's message, matched by its code, and frees the file previews. It removes the message from those waiting to send and leaves a note so an older copy cannot bring it back.
steps.detail: The HTTP response or WebSocket message.created event updates the replica and removes the optimistic entry by nonce. File previews are released and durable removal creates an outbox tombstone.

flows.detail: The visible draft, durable local work and server message each have different owners. Sending connects them with a nonce and acknowledgement rather than merely clearing the textarea.

flows.title: Picking up after a lost connection or restart
flows.summary: When something goes wrong, the app tells three cases apart. It may not know whether a message arrived, the server may have refused it, or an attached file may no longer be on the device, and in every case the same words must never quietly post twice.

steps.title: Show what went wrong
steps.description: A message that failed stays in the conversation, marked as sending, with the reason and what you can do. If the server refused it, it waits until you choose Retry. If the app cannot tell whether it arrived, it keeps the same code, so the server can spot a repeat.
steps.detail: A failed send stays in pending state with an actionable reason. A known refusal requires deliberate Retry; an uncertain outcome retains the same nonce.

steps.title: Note each change before saving it
steps.description: Before the app saves a change in the browser's storage, it first writes a quick note of the change. If the save fails or the page closes, the note stays and the change is made the next time the app starts. Each note records which tab made it and in what order, so a change already saved is never made twice.
steps.detail: deviceStore synchronously records the storage operation, then commits an IndexedDB transaction. Failure keeps the journal entry; tab/sequence metadata prevents repeating an operation already committed.

steps.title: Check the workspace before restoring
steps.description: The app restores saved work only after the server confirms which workspace and account this is, and the address is approved. It then reads the saved work for exactly that workspace and account. If the saved work cannot be read, the app offers to try again rather than starting empty.
steps.detail: The ready snapshot identifies workspace/account, WorkspaceStorageGate admits the address, and workspaceStorage reads the correct versioned keys. Unreadable storage offers retry instead of an empty alternate store.

steps.title: Restore unsent messages or their words
steps.description: The app restores messages saved as waiting to send and sends them again. Where the device kept only the words, they come back as text, unless that message was already sent or discarded. A message whose files are gone, or that is too old to resend on its own, waits for you to decide.
steps.detail: Durable outbox records restore sends; unstored recovery records restore words only when the outbox/tombstone does not own the nonce. Missing files and sends beyond the retry window remain held for the author.

steps.title: Catch up without a flood of notifications
steps.description: On reconnecting, the app tells the server the last update it saw and gets everything it missed, matched against the history it already has. Missed messages that still matter arrive as one catch-up summary instead of many notifications. A missed @here does not ring, since it was meant for people around at the time.
steps.detail: WebSocket hello sends lastSeq, replay is reconciled with snapshot-watermarked history, and eligible missed messages become a catch-up summary. @here replay is not treated as live presence.

flows.detail: Recovery distinguishes unknown network outcome, explicit server refusal and unavailable local attachment bytes. The same text must not silently become two sends.

flows.title: Using Tandem in two windows at once
flows.summary: When two windows save at once, Tandem merges each change in on its own, so neither window wipes out the other's drafts or deletions. The parts of the app that use these saves must still handle late answers themselves.

steps.title: Pick one place to save
steps.description: In a browser, the app keeps drafts and choices in one storage place and records that choice before moving older saved work into it. It does not switch places just because the browser cannot message other windows. If storage will not open, the app says it cannot be read and offers to try again.
steps.detail: N02 persists IndexedDB ownership before migration. Missing BroadcastChannel does not change ownership; failed opening remains unreadability with retry.

steps.title: Save only what changed
steps.description: Each save changes one thing in a single step, such as one conversation's draft, one message waiting to send, or one account's choice. If two windows typed different words into the same draft, the app keeps both. A message already sent or discarded cannot be brought back by an older copy.
steps.detail: A readwrite transaction merges one conversation's draft, one nonce's outbox state or one account's choice. Draft bases preserve conflicting words, and outbox tombstones/floors reject stale resurrection.

steps.title: Tell the other windows
steps.description: The app tells the other open windows what changed. If the usual route is missing, a backup signal names only what changed, and the other window reads it from storage. Windows also check again when you switch to them, and ignore late answers to older requests.
steps.detail: BroadcastChannel can deliver the change; a fallback storage event carries only the changed key, then reads IndexedDB. Focus refresh and generation guards supplement that path.

steps.title: Update the other window without losing its edits
steps.description: The other window takes in new drafts and messages waiting to send, without overwriting words you are still typing there. It also picks up a change to whether notifications show message previews. Edits you make there afterwards still merge correctly.
steps.detail: DraftPersistence adopts another window's drafts/outbox without overwriting its still-unsaved edits, while notification preview watchers update privacy choice. Newer local edits retain their own merge base.

steps.title: Three ways windows used to clash
steps.description: Three problems of this kind were repaired. Two windows opening a workspace at a new address at the same moment can no longer both trust it.
